# reg_def

**Compile-time MCU register definitions and access code, generated by the C preprocessor.**

`reg_def` is a header-only C/C++ library for describing MCU and peripheral register sets
in a declarative, data-sheet-like style and generating the register access and
manipulation code automatically using the standard C preprocessor.

- **Header only.** Drop in the headers and `#include "reg_def.h"`. No build step, no dependencies
  beyond `<stdbool.h>` / `<stdint.h>`.
- **Zero runtime cost.** Masks, shifts, and field composition are computed by the
  preprocessor and constant-folded by the compiler.
- **Data-sheet-friendly syntax.** Registers and fields are declared the way they appear in
  an MCU manual.  This makes it easier to work with code and datasheets side-by-side.
- **Bus-agnostic.** Memory-mapped, I²C, SPI, magic-write registers — you supply three
  tiny access functions per register *type*; the library generates everything else
  and user code sees the same register access API.
- **Multi-instance.** Address the same register set across several device instances,
  (I²C addresses, base pointers, …) through one API.

## Quick start

`reg_def` by itself doesn't know how to touch the hardware, so we first have to define a register
type and its accessor functions.  For example, here is a memory-mapped 8-bit register,
which resides in the flat address space that is directly accessible by the CPU:

```c
#include "reg_def.h"

#define mem_reg8(reg_name, addr, ...) \
  reg_def_inline void     set_ ## reg_name ## _raw_reg_value (uint8_t v) { *(volatile uint8_t*)addr = v; } \
  reg_def_inline uint8_t  get_ ## reg_name ## _raw_reg_value (void)      { return *(volatile uint8_t*)addr; } \
  reg_def_inline void     rmw_ ## reg_name (uint8_t a, uint8_t o)        { *(volatile uint8_t*)addr = (*(volatile uint8_t*)addr & a) | o; } \
  expand_define_reg (reg_name, uint8_t, __VA_ARGS__)
```

That macro provides the three low-level functions (`set_/get_..._raw_reg_value`, `rmw_...`)
and hands the field list (via va-args) to `expand_define_reg`, which generates the masks and field
helpers. With this in place, we can declare registers and their bitfields in a straight forward and easy to read way:

```c
mem_reg8 (ADC_B_CONTROL, 0xFF0E,

  // reg_bits (field name, high bit, low bit, value type)
  reg_bits (start_running, 7, 7, bool),
  reg_bits (test,          6, 6, bool),
  reg_bits (mode,          5, 5, enum adc_b_mode),
  reg_bits (en_interrupt,  4, 4, bool),
  reg_bits (bias_adj,      2, 1, enum adc_bias_adj_val),
  reg_bits (ck_sel,        0, 0, enum adc_b_ck_sel_val)
)
```

Register access goes through a unified functional-looking macro API, regardless of the underlying register type:

```c
// read the whole register
uint8_t raw = get_reg (ADC_B_CONTROL);

// read a single field from the register
bool    irq = get_reg (ADC_B_CONTROL, en_interrupt);

// read-modify-write the the specified fields (other bits preserved)
set_reg (ADC_B_CONTROL,
  (start_running, true),
  (mode,          adc_b_continuous));

// overwrite the whole register from named fields (no read before write)
reset_reg (ADC_B_CONTROL,
  (start_running, true),
  (mode,          adc_b_continuous),
  (en_interrupt,  false));

// write a raw value directly
reset_reg (ADC_B_CONTROL, 0x11);

// raw read-modify-write: (value & and_mask) | or_mask
rmw_reg (ADC_B_CONTROL, 0xF0, 0x0A);
```

## Access API

| Macro | Reads HW? | Writes HW? | Purpose |
|-------|:---------:|:----------:|---------|
| `get_reg (reg [, field])` | ✅ | — | Read the register; extract a field, or the raw value. |
| `set_reg (reg, (field, val), …)` | ✅ | ✅ | Read-modify-write the named fields, preserving the rest. |
| `reset_reg (reg, (field, val), …)` | — | ✅ | Overwrite the whole register from named fields. |
| `reset_reg (reg, rawval)` | — | ✅ | Overwrite the whole register with a raw value. |
| `rmw_reg (reg, and_mask, or_mask)` | ✅ | ✅ | Raw read-modify-write: `(v & and_mask) \| or_mask`. |
| `make_reg_value (reg, (field, val), …)` | — | — | Compose a raw value from fields; no HW touched. |
| `get_reg_value (val, reg [, field])` | — | — | Extract a field from a value in memory. |
| `set_reg_value (val, reg, (field, val), …)` | — | — | Set fields in a value variable in memory. |

### Split / scattered bitfields
Fields that are split across non-adjacent bits are declared with `reg_bits_2` and accessed
as one contiguous value:

```c
mem_reg8 (EXAMPLE_REG, 0xFF00,
  // split 3 + 2 bit field layout: 'xxx...yy'
  // read/written as a 5-bit value 'xxxyy'
  reg_bits_2 (scattered, 7, 5, 1, 0, uint8_t)
)
```

### Multiple device instances

For several devices sharing one register layout but distinguished by an address (I²C
address, base pointer, …), pass a `(reg_name, instance)` tuple as the first argument. The
macros dispatch to `_1`-suffixed low-level functions that take the instance as a leading
parameter (define those alongside the plain ones):

```c
bool b = get_reg ((AW9523B_INPUT_PORT0,  0x58), p0_3);
set_reg          ((AW9523B_OUTPUT_PORT0, 0x5B), (p0_3, true));
rmw_reg          ((AW9523B_OUTPUT_PORT0, 0x5B), 0xF0, 0x0A);
```

The instance token is just passed through by the macros, so it can be anything,
like a constant address or variable.

## Installation

Copy `reg_def.h` **and** the `reg_def_pp_utils/` folder into your project, then include the
main header:

```c
#include "reg_def.h"
```

`reg_def.h` pulls its preprocessor helpers from `reg_def_pp_utils/` (`pp_utils.h`,
`pp_args.h`, `pp_for_each.h`) automatically — no include-path setup required.

### Using it in a project that already has the pp_* utilities

If your project already has the pp_* utilities `reg_def` can be pointed to
use those instead of the bundled ones by definiing the `REG_DEF_PP_FOR_EACH_H` macro.
For example:

```sh
gcc -DREG_DEF_PP_FOR_EACH_H='"utils/pp_for_each.h"' ...
```

`reg_def.h` includes only `pp_for_each.h` directly (which pulls in the other two), so this
one macro redirects the whole dependency.

## How it works

- The `pp_*.h` headers are a minimial preprocessor-metaprogramming toolkit
  (`pp_for_each`, `pp_args_size`, token pasting, …) used to iterate over the `reg_bits`
  list.
- `expand_define_reg` generates, per register: an `enum <reg>_bits` of bit/value masks and
  the hardware-independent field helpers (`make_`, `set1_`, `get_..._value_`).
- The high-level `get_reg` / `set_reg` / `reset_reg` / `rmw_reg` main API macros compose those
  helpers with the three low-level user defined access functions per register type:

  ```c
  void         set_<reg>_raw_reg_value (<raw_type> v);
  <raw_type>   get_<reg>_raw_reg_value (void);
  void         rmw_<reg> (<raw_type> and_mask, <raw_type> or_mask);
  ```

  Everything is wired together by token pasting on these exact names, so any register bus
  (memory-mapped, I²C, SPI, the WDT's magic-write scheme, …) is just a new device macro
  that provides those three functions and calls `expand_define_reg`. See `example.c` for
  `mem_reg8/16/32` and a magic-write `wdt_reg8` you can copy.

## Compiler support

Tested with **GCC**, **G++** and **SDCC**.
C11 or C++11 is required for `static_assert` usage in the library.
